## #2 — Meshman — 2007-07-02

[[QUOTE:  poula_jones said: Hi friend I am a new learner of cheetah 3d, I like this program because it is much easier then other 3d softwares. But I have a question about the taking it for career. Is anybody t]]

Hi poula, I don't know if you'd be able to use it on a course (I'd imagine that a lot of courses use specific software to standardise things a bit) but you'll certainly learn a lot of basic 3d software principals quite quickly with cheetah and you'll find that picking up other software packages will become easier as a result.  If you want to pursue a career in animation you'll ultimately need to learn the industry standards such as Maya and Softimage but I don't see there is any harm in starting off with what you find comfortable.  Animation is more about technique than the software at the end of the day anyway.  Just my 2c worth.

MM

## #3 — Margus16 — 2007-07-03
<https://www.cheetah3d.com/forum/index.php?threads/1883/post-12986>

Hello
As you said, its more easy than other 3 software, it looks to me you are a beginner. Before thinking about career, try to figure out what kind of models come out well. Maybe your vehicles are just a junk but architecture comes out very well. Who knows. Then think a bit where you can use your skills. Then i suggest you to work in a game modding team for a while. (usually they dont pay for you). You will get much knowlege and skills. 
I suggest you to lear other programs too. C3d is easy and userfriendly and very great 3d program (specially for beginners), but if you gain more skills you might find some tools missing. But its only the matter of time until c3d gets these. Martin works really fast:icon_thumbup:. And olso, you cant use it when you go to somewhere to learn 3d. They mostly use Maya which is unfortunately very difficult. I even dont dare to try it.
Good luck
